topic: Adding polygon geometry to facility data
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on adding polygon geometry (specifically for 'zone' facility types) to the company 7906 data. Initial concerns were raised about storing large, text-based fields in existing asset tables.

It was suggested that using a PostgreSQL native field type like `geometry` or `geography` would be ideal. If this is not possible, storing the geometry as WKT (Well-Known Text) format is an acceptable alternative. If WKT is used, precision limits must be agreed upon.

Regarding the existing facility geometry field, it was noted that it is currently only used for calculating distances to the nearest point. However, a need arose to potentially calculate distances between polygons as well.

Finally, the required coordinate precision was determined to be sufficient if it is less than one meter.
decisions: Polygon geometry will be added to facility data for company 7906.
The preferred storage method for polygon geometry is a PostgreSQL native field (`geometry`/`geography`).
If using WKT format, the required coordinate precision must be set to less than one meter.
action_items: Investigate feasibility of storing polygon geometry in asset tables without bloating them.
Determine if distance calculation between polygons will be required.
